clue.text: Don't waver if you want to get on your feet quickly

definitions.meaning: an injunction to hold firm and not give ground

definitions.text: if you want to get on your feet quickly
definitions.meaning: read literally, rise upright without delay

explanation.surface: Advice to stay resolute, with a hint about standing up briskly.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold firm is to refuse to yield; read literally the phrase is an order to rise rapidly.

clue.text: Catch on what rose pickers are likely to catch on

definitions.meaning: to grasp or understand something, informally

definitions.text: what rose pickers are likely to catch on
definitions.meaning: the small thorny shoots of a bush snag the gatherer's sleeves

explanation.surface: Gardeners picking roses keep snagging on the bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang for understanding; also a small shoot of a branch that snags clothing.

clue.text: Mean grading needs changing

indicators.note: something that needs changing will be altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teacher's average marks are unfair and should be revised.
explanation.definitionFit: A miserly, stingy person is mean with money.

clue.text: Totally exhausted from working at full capacity

definitions.meaning: completely tired out, spent
going at maximum speed or effort

explanation.surface: A worker driven to collapse by going all out.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both worn out and at maximum effort or speed.

clue.text: Help me love! It's only fair

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal asking for help
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A lovesick plea followed by a lukewarm verdict on the romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Middling or mediocre, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Retired after being sent abroad as a police informer

parts.note: put out means sent out or dispatched away
to grass is British slang for informing to the police

explanation.surface: An informer is packed off overseas for his own safety.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a grass is a police informer. The idiom describes a horse or worker pensioned off.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is used of an old horse turned into a field, and so of a person pensioned off from work.

clue.text: Risk total defeat at Wimbledon

parts.note: to invite catastrophe, with a nod to the tennis courts of the famous tournament

explanation.surface: A tennis player is heading for a humiliating loss.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship, played on courts; to court something is to invite it.
explanation.definitionFit: To invite catastrophe, punning on the tennis court.

clue.text: Predominant interest is suppressing carnal desire

parts.note: ruling means controlling or holding in check
passion is strong sexual desire

explanation.surface: A moralist's chief concern is keeping lust in check.
explanation.definitionFit: A dominant enthusiasm or obsession that governs someone's life.

clue.text: Losing it would make a fat woman lean and weary

definitions.text: Losing it would make a fat woman

parts.note: spare can mean thin or lean
to weary is to tire

explanation.surface: A dieting woman, slimmed down but worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the first stretch: losing a roll of belly fat makes a woman slimmer; 'lean' is a piece, not the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocular term for a roll of flab round the waist, likened to a car's extra wheel.

clue.text: How a royal warrant is given to protect the chassis from rust

definitions.text: How a royal warrant is given
definitions.meaning: an official document issued with the sovereign's stamp

definitions.text: to protect the chassis from rust
definitions.meaning: a coating applied beneath a car's body

explanation.surface: A royally approved anti-rust treatment for cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Documents issued authenticated by a stamp; also a protective coating for a vehicle's underside.

clue.text: Part of ship unaffected when it capsizes

indicators.note: a word unchanged when turned end to end reads the same in both directions

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A ship's structure that survives being overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: The raised deck at the stern is the part meant; the word reads the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised deck at a sailing vessel's stern.

clue.text: To be taken for a ride was wearing

definitions.text: To be taken for a ride
definitions.meaning: to be fooled or tricked
had clothing on the body

explanation.surface: Someone duped while dressed for a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for tricked or deceived; also, literally, wore clothes.

clue.text: Gold article found on the Algerian coast

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Treasure discovered on a North African beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A port city in north-west Algeria on the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Appropriate attire given to an English saint

parts.note: an alb is a white vestment, fitting dress for a cleric

explanation.surface: Suitable clothing presented to a holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's first Christian martyr, honoured at St Albans.

clue.text: Archetypal pickpocket caught smoking?

parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette
in means caught or held within

explanation.surface: A thief caught having a sneaky cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: Fag is British slang for a cigarette; someone caught with one in is smoking. The answer is the thief master in Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's master thief in Oliver Twist, who trains boys to steal.

clue.text: What the American viper did when considerably alarmed

definitions.meaning: a New World pit viper shakes its tail to make a warning noise
unnerved, shaken up

explanation.surface: A frightened snake gives its warning.
explanation.definitionFit: The snake shook its tail; also, informally, flustered or unnerved.

clue.text: Tense description of a duck walk is sheer nonsense

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
a duck's gait is a waddle

explanation.surface: Calling a duck's gait tense is utter rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly, trivial talk or writing.

clue.text: Also abstain from eating at an excessive rate

parts.note: too means also
to fast is to go without food

explanation.surface: Advice not to eat or to wolf food down.
explanation.definitionFit: Speeding, with more velocity than is sensible.

clue.text: The land needs to soak up heaven-sent water

annotationWithheld.why: The land needs to soak up heaven-sent water: 'The land' defines it and RAIN is 'heaven-sent water', but no clue words give TER, and 'soak up' fits no container; the clue may be misprinted
annotationWithheld.clue: The land needs to soak up heaven-sent water

clue.text: Investigates a saint upsetting the clergy

parts.note: pries means pokes into or investigates

indicators.note: upsetting means overturning, so the abbreviation is read in the other direction

explanation.surface: Someone probes a holy figure in a way that offends churchmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordained ministers, collectively forming the clergy.

clue.text: Writer going to Jerusalem gets a living allowance

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
Sion, or Zion, is a poetic name for Jerusalem

explanation.surface: An author moving to Israel receives a grant.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular retirement payment to live on.

clue.text: Not well cooked, but that is unusual

definitions.meaning: of meat, only lightly done
uncommon, seldom seen

explanation.surface: A steak that is undercooked is a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Of meat, red inside and lightly done; also, uncommon.

clue.text: Make hot iron

definitions.meaning: a make is a trade name for a product
a piece of burning wood or a heated marker for livestock

explanation.surface: An instruction to heat metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade label of goods; also a heated marking tool or torch.

clue.text: A single and a first class return to the continent

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for single, as on forms

indicators.note: return means go back, so these letters are read in the other direction

parts.note: A1 means first class, written with I for the figure one

explanation.surface: A traveller buys a one-way and a first-class round-trip ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-rate, written AI; turned round it gives IA. 'Single' and 'return' look like ticket types.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest landmass, stretching from the Urals to the Pacific.

clue.text: Part of Ireland could possibly appeal

parts.note: may expresses possibility
O is an exclamation of appeal, as in O Lord

explanation.surface: An Irish county might plead for something.
explanation.definitionFit: A county in the west of the Republic, in Connacht.

clue.text: Complaint of a couple leaving Prague

indicators.note: leaving means departing from, so these letters are taken out of the city's name

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair, a couple

explanation.surface: Two tourists fall ill and go home from the Czech capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A malarial fever, an old-fashioned name for an illness.

clue.text: A reservation is needed for all the way to the terminus

definitions.meaning: a qualifying phrase limiting how far a statement holds

definitions.text: all the way to the terminus
definitions.meaning: literally, right to the end of the line

explanation.surface: A traveller books a seat to the end of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom expressing a qualification; literally, up to the end point of a route.

clue.text: Where Australians are apparently feather-bedded

definitions.meaning: an informal term for Australia and New Zealand
lying beneath a quilt of soft plumage

explanation.surface: Australians enjoy a cushy life.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal name for the Antipodes; literally, beneath soft plumage as in a quilt.
